title: Edward Clem and Buddy Bolden
summary: Parker recalls trumpeter Edward Clem and Buddy Bolden as blues king, reading and playing at Dixie Park.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: This fella, Reed, he brought you Norm Good, too. I seen his name in the book yesterday, uh... Edward Clem. You know Edward Clem.
I've heard of him plenty. Uh-huh. I've heard of him plenty. Ernest Rogers used to talk about him. Yeah, Ernest. Ernest used to play with you.
Oh, yeah? Yeah, Ernest Rogers? Yes. I don't tell him. Yeah. Oh, yeah. He's from down here. How did Edward Clem play?
Huh? How did Edward Clem play?
Edward?
Clem?
Who is Clem? Yeah.
How?
Huh?
What kind of music did he play? Uh, Clem Boy? Edward Glim. Oh, the trumpet.
Trumpet player.
Was he ratty or was he...
Ratty, yeah, he's ratty.
Yes.

Did he read? Yeah. He read all good. Good musicians. This fella, you know him too, you heard him. Buddy Bowling. Yes. Oh, he was a blues king. Yes. He brought them blues out. Old Buddy Bowling. Old Buddy Bowling. Buddy Bowling. I don't know why he comes. Somewhere out of the country. What did he play like? Did he play... Buddy Bowling. He played lots of blues, you say?
Oh, he played a blues. What? Mm-hm.
Mm-hm.
Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.

Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. See, out here at the Harmon Park, not the Harmon Park, but the Dixie Park, they have two fences. They have one at this park and one over there. And the old muddy boy would get to the window and put that horn to his head. Boy, before you know that place would be packed. I don't know about the border. All he got poisoned he did was a little one.
What tunes did he play? What tunes did he play? Did he have his own tunes?
Different tunes. Different things.
Great. Could he read music?
Yeah, he could read. Yeah, all of them could read. You know how a fella picked up an engine and couldn't read. Pick up an engine and went to school right away.
What, uh, who was in his band? Who played with him? Did he have a trombone player?

I'm stuck now who was in trouble. Oh, yeah, you know him too. What's his name again? He comes from up in the Tess water. Big old, big fella. Big old, big fella. He was a trombone player. He died up there. I just remember his name. And he was a buddy boy with a trombone player. And who else was in the band?
Oh, dude, fellas. I don't know what I was.
I know him but I can't think of who I was.
